subject: Post-demo recap & rate-card questions for Nova Health dedicated lanes
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap & rate-card questions for Nova Health dedicated lanes

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap and the three items we need to close pricing properly:  

Call highlights (short):
- Nova Health runbook: patient-facing summarization + internal knowledge retrieval.
- Baseline monthly tokens: you indicated ~800M baseline with growth to 1.5B+ in peak months.
- Latency target: 99th percentile sub-350ms for short completion paths (~<256 tokens).
- Preferred hardware: H100 preferred for dense MT/LLM workloads but open to A100 if economics force a trade.

Open items we need from your side to finalize a dedicated-lane estimate:
1) Confirm a 30 / 90 day token velocity distribution (baseline vs peak month). You mentioned seasonal spikes tied to specific campaigns — can you share approximate monthly numbers for the next 6 months?
2) Budget range for committed reserved lanes (monthly): you gave a ballpark $40k-$60k earlier — confirm if that is firm or aspirational.
3) Procurement timeline & legal: target PO/contract month (e.g., Apr, May) and any procurement constraints (PO required, self-serve billing not allowed, required SLAs).

What I attached: nova-dedicated-estimate-v1.pdf (high-level lanes & unit economics) and a simple XLS scenario showing pricing per 1M tokens across lane sizes.

Preliminary pricing note (we'll refine once we have the items above): for H100 reserved lanes we typically show a 2-lane starter and 4-lane scale path. Example ballpark: 2 H100 lanes (reserved) ~ $34.5k/mo committed, 4 lanes ~ $64k/mo committed (example with 12mo commit and standard enterprise discount). At ~1.5B tokens/mo that maps to roughly $23-24 / 1M tokens for the 2-lane scenario (illustrative). We'll run exact math once you confirm monthly volumes.

Next steps: please reply with the 3 items above; I'll follow up with a two-option firm quote (2-lane + 4-lane) and a short cost-per-1M tokens table showing sensitivity to token volume and lane count. If helpful, we can lock a follow-up 30-minute call Thursday or Friday this week.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: nova-dedicated-estimate-v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@novahealth.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nova Health Procurement <procurement@novahealth.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & rate-card questions for Nova Health dedicated lanes

Olga — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline:  

1) Monthly volumes: current baseline ~800M tokens/mo (steady-state). We expect campaigns in May/Oct to push to 1.4–1.6B tokens in peak months. For modeling please use a 6-month ramp: 800M, 850M, 950M, 1.1B, 1.3B, 1.5B.
2) Budget: leadership signaled target is $30k–$45k/mo (closer to $40k ideal). $60k would be tough without clear justification on latency improvements / SLA.
3) Procurement: target contract start earliest May 1 — procurement will require a formal quote + SOW, standard PO process (Net 45). They also request SOC2 attestation and data residency within US regions.

Hardware: we prefer H100, but we will entertain A100 if price delta is >20% and performance impact is minimal. Also curious if Redwood supports int8/quantized profiles for model family X (we will likely push for quantized 8-bit to reduce costs).

Can you provide modeled $/1M tokens for both a 2-lane and 4-lane H100 committed path (12-month term) and for an A100 fallback? Please include the math/assumptions (peak vs baseline amortization).

Jordan Park
Director, Product — Nova Health
jordan.park@novahealth.ai
Phone: (415) 555-0182

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & rate-card questions for Nova Health dedicated lanes — modeled scenarios

Jordan — appreciate the detail. Per your ask, attached is a concise modeled comparison (see lane-pricing-scenarios.xlsx) plus the PDF estimate. Below I summarize the modeled math and assumptions so you can share with procurement quickly.

Assumptions used for the scenarios:
- Latency target: 99p <350ms; model family X (2k context typical), standard batching for low-latency routing.
- Baseline / peak volumes: used your provided 6-mo ramp; we amortize committed monthly cost across the month token volume (typical accounting for reserved lanes).
- Committed discount: 12-month commit used in these scenarios (we can show month-to-month but pricing is ~20% higher).
- Quantization: we support int8-like profiles for model family X; A100 quantization effectiveness varies — we modeled conservative 15% throughput improvement on H100 with int8.

Scenario A — 2 H100 reserved lanes (12mo commit):
- Committed cost: $34,500 / month (includes reserved capacity + enterprise tooling + 10% commit discount).
- Example month (1.5B tokens): cost per 1M tokens = $34,500 / 1500 = $23.00 / 1M tokens.
- At baseline month (800M tokens): cost per 1M tokens = $34,500 / 800 = $43.13 / 1M tokens.

Scenario B — 4 H100 reserved lanes (12mo commit):
- Committed cost: $64,000 / month.
- At 1.5B tokens (assuming lanes used to handle peak burst capacity across requests): cost per 1M tokens = $64,000 / 1500 = $42.67 / 1M tokens.
- If you amortize across higher sustained volume (e.g., 3B tokens), cost falls to ~$21.33 / 1M tokens.

A100 fallback (2 lanes, 12mo commit):
- Committed cost estimate: $28,000 / month (lower raw lane price).
- At 1.5B tokens: ~ $18.67 / 1M tokens.
- Note: A100 may require larger lane counts or different batching to hit your 99p latency target depending on model tuning; cost delta vs H100 should be weighed against SLAs.

Observations & recommended approach:
- If Nova expects the 6-month ramp to hit 1.3–1.5B tokens regularly, a 4-lane commitment with a consumption plan or tiered burst credits will produce the lowest $/1M token once volume is realized.
- If near-term budget is constrained to ~$40k/mo, a 2-lane H100 commit with quoted reserved credits + burst overlay is the pragmatic path — it gives headroom for bursts while staying within your near-term finance guardrails.
- We can also model a hybrid: 2 reserved H100 lanes + 1 ephemeral A100 lane for elastic peak handling; the attached XLS has that scenario in tab 'Hybrid'.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will prepare a firm two-option quote (2-lane H100 committed; 4-lane H100 committed) with explicit SLA language, PO instructions, and a small burst credit add-on you can use while procurement completes.
2) If acceptable, propose we target a signature window the week of Apr 18 to meet your May 1 start (procurement timeline accounted).
3) Confirm whether the procurement team needs SOC2 evidence sent directly to procurement@novahealth.ai or uploaded to an SSO portal.

Available times for a 30-minute follow-up: Thu 3/18 10am PT or Fri 3/19 11am PT — let me know which works and I'll lock it.

Thanks — attaching the two files and the model.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachments: nova-dedicated-estimate-v1.pdf (PDF), lane-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (XLSX)]
